title: The receptive helper verb (passive)
summary: れる / られる means "to receive or get" the action of the verb before it. The receiver is the main carriage, and the real doer is marked with に.

blocks.text: Textbooks call this the "passive" and label it a conjugation. The course prefers **receptive helper verb**, because that is what it does: it makes a verb that means "to get" or "to receive" the action. Both names point at the same form. What matters is that the particles keep doing their usual jobs.
Attach the helper to the **あ-stem** (the same stem ない uses). Godan: **れる**. Ichidan: **られる**. It looks exactly like the ichidan potential られる, but real sentences make the difference clear.

The engine of the sentence is **れる / られる**, so the main carriage is the one who **receives**. It does not have to be a person. The real doer is marked with **に**. The picture: れる is a **pull** verb, so に marks the **source** the thing is pulled from, not a target.

blocks.en: The water got drunk by the dog.

blocks.jp: かばんが誰かに盗まれた。
blocks.en: The bag was stolen by someone.

blocks.text: Japanese also uses the receptive when something happens **to a person** and it bothers them. The affected person becomes the main carriage (が), while the thing that was taken keeps its **を**.

blocks.jp: さくらが誰かにかばんを盗まれた。
blocks.en: Sakura had her bag stolen by someone.

blocks.text: Keep the receptive in **two separate verbs**: the head verb れる / られる belongs to the receiver, the attached verb is done by someone else. Unlike the potential, they must never be merged into one.

items: **あ-stem + れる** (godan), **られる** (ichidan): "to get X-ed".
The **receiver** is the main carriage (**が**). The **doer** takes **に**.
The suffering receptive: **person が + other に + thing を + 〜られた**.
Do not mix it up with the potential: **食べられる** can be either, and the sentence tells you which.

questions.instruction: Who is the main carriage in 水が犬に飲まれた?
questions.note: The one who receives the action is the main carriage.

questions.instruction: Tap the doer (who did the drinking)
questions.note: に marks the doer in a receptive sentence.

questions.prompt: The bag was stolen by someone.
questions.note: Receiver が, doer に, receptive verb.

questions.instruction: Which means "Sakura had her bag stolen" (it bothered her)?
options: さくらが誰かにかばんを盗まれた
さくらが誰かにかばんが盗んだ
さくらを誰かにかばんが盗まれた
さくらは誰かをかばんに盗まれた
questions.note: The affected person takes が; the stolen thing keeps を.

questions.prompt: In a receptive sentence, に can mark who did the action.
questions.note: れる is a pull verb: に marks where the action comes from.

questions.instruction: Which ending does an ichidan verb take for the receptive?
questions.note: 食べる → 食べられる.

questions.instruction: Which stem does the receptive attach to?
questions.note: The same stem as ない.

questions.instruction: What does 食べられる mean here?
options: The fish got eaten by the cat
The fish could eat the cat
The cat can eat the fish
questions.note: Receiver 魚が, doer 猫に: the receptive, not the potential.

questions.instruction: Why must the receptive not be merged into one engine?
options: It has two verbs with two different doers
questions.note: The receiver owns れる; someone else does the attached verb.

questions.instruction: Which sentence is about a thing getting something done to it?
questions.note: 窓が割られた: the window got broken (by someone).
